question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for host tools: a deny-wins `tools.fs` allow/deny PathGuard policy, a root/access-mode policy, or a narrower workspace-only plus separate exec policy?
rationale: This choice defines a public config surface and security boundary, and current open implementation candidates make different tradeoffs around exec, compatibility, and false-security risk.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence coverage, and make exec coverage explicit before merging any implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate boundary
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state that shell-mediated filesystem access remains a separate security boundary.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Close or downgrade the config request only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own host filesystem path ACLs beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence coverage, and make exec coverage explicit before merging any implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest review and git-history signal on the current workspaceOnly policy and prior maintainer framing for this issue.
